notes: Replaces the earlier Rolls-Royce Motor Cars edit, whose owner (BMW) three of the four models missed. Disney's ownership of Lucasfilm is far better known. The relation is direct_subsidiary_of (functional, a subproperty of the transitive subsidiary_of), which gives functional (related near), transitivity through Industrial Light & Magic (related far, stored: Wikipedia states that Disney acquired ILM as part of Lucasfilm; the subsidiary_of bridge makes the chain subproperty then transitivity), and subproperty twice (shared owner with Columbia Pictures; an investor's indirect stake, as an application: the rule speaks of subsidiaries, so the direct-subsidiary edit must first become subsidiary_of). Disney's units such as Lucasfilm sit under Walt Disney Studios, a division rather than a company, so the Walt Disney Company is the immediate parent company. Negation asked as "Is it true that ... not ...?" rather than "Is it false that ...?", which two models misread in the audit. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama) except those marked approximate (AND queries, max_clause_freq 500000). The shared-owner question says 'ultimately owned' (Columbia's immediate owner is Sony Pictures Entertainment, a Sony group company). 'Parent company' follows common usage (the Walt Disney Company; the studio division in between is not counted as a company). The quote for the ILM claim was taken from the review of this record, not re-fetched (Wikipedia and infini-gram refused further requests).
